subject: Two age classes in a multi-state model using multinomial likelihood

messages.subject: Two age classes in a multi-state model using multinomial likelihood
parts:
Hello all,

I am currently working on an age-specific multi-state model with multinomial likelihood. The dataset comprises information from >3500 marked vultures of various ages, incorporating recaptures and observations both within and outside our study site, along with dead recoveries spanning 29 occasions. The primary objective is to estimate the site-specific survival rates for two age classes: non-adults (0 to 4 years) and adults (>4 years). The states are encoded as follows: alive as a non-adult at site A (1), alive as an adult at site A (2), alive as a non-adult at site B (3), alive as an adult at site B (4), and recovered dead (5).

Here is the code and .csv:

library(jagsUI) library(IPMbook)

MS <- read.table("CAT_5states.csv", header=T, sep=",")

marr <- marray(MS, unobs = 1)

# Bundle data
# There are 5 states in MS but we added an non-observable state "6"
# to calculate the absorbing state or long-dead state.
mns <- 6
jags.data <- list(marr=marr, n.occasions=ncol(MS), relm=rowSums(marr), mns=mns, zerom=matrix(0, mns, mns),
                  onesm=diag(mns), recap = c(rep(1,3),2:29)) # first two occasions there were no recaptures

sink("marray.jags")
cat("
model {

# Priors and linear models
  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    logit(s1.cat[t]) <- suv1.cat + epsilon1.cat[t]
      epsilon1.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(s2.cat[t]) <- suv2.cat + epsilon2.cat[t]
      epsilon2.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(s1.oth[t]) <- suv1.oth + epsilon1.oth[t]
      epsilon1.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(s2.oth[t]) <- suv2.oth + epsilon2.oth[t]
      epsilon2.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(p1.cat[t]) <- rec1.cat[recap[t]] + gamma1.cat[recap[t]]
      gamma1.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(p2.cat[t]) <- rec2.cat[recap[t]] + gamma2.cat[recap[t]]
      gamma2.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(p1.oth[t]) <- rec1.oth + gamma1.oth[t]
      gamma1.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(p2.oth[t]) <- rec2.oth + gamma2.oth[t]
      gamma2.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(r[t]) <- recov + delta[t]
      delta[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.r)
    F[t] <- mean.F
  }

for (i in 2:(n.occasions-1)){
 rec1.cat[i] <- logit(mean1.p.cat)
 rec2.cat[i] <- logit(mean2.p.cat)
}
 
suv1.cat <- logit(mean1.suv.cat)
suv2.cat <- logit(mean2.suv.cat)
suv1.oth <- logit(mean1.suv.oth)
suv2.oth <- logit(mean2.suv.oth)
rec1.cat[1] <- 0                 #First two occasions on CAT set to 0
rec2.cat[1] <- 0 #First two occasions on OTH set to 0 rec1.oth <- logit(mean1.p.oth)
rec2.oth <- logit(mean2.p.oth)
recov <- logit(mean.recov)
mean1.suv.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean1.suv.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.suv.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.suv.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean1.p.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean1.p.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.p.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.p.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean.recov ~ dunif(0, 1)

tau.s <- pow(sigma.s, -2)
sigma.s ~ dunif(0, 10)
sigma2.s <- pow(sigma.s, 2)

tau.p <- pow(sigma.p, -2)
sigma.p ~ dunif(0, 10)
sigma2.p <- pow(sigma.p, 2)

tau.r <- pow(sigma.r, -2)
sigma.r ~ dunif(0, 10)
sigma2.r <- pow(sigma.r, 2)

# Transitions: gamma priors
   for (i in 1:2){
    a[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
    psiC[i] <- a[i]/sum(a[])
    d[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
    psiO[i] <- d[i]/sum(d[])
   }
 
# Define state-transition and re-encounter probabilities
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
  psm[1,t,1] <- s1.cat[t]*psiC[1]
  psm[1,t,2] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[1]
  psm[1,t,3] <- s1.cat[t]*psiC[2]
  psm[1,t,4] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[2]
  psm[1,t,5] <- (1-s1.cat[t])*r[t]
  psm[1,t,6] <- (1-s1.cat[t])*(1-r[t])
  psm[2,t,1] <- 0
  psm[2,t,2] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[1]
  psm[2,t,3] <- 0
  psm[2,t,4] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[2]
  psm[2,t,5] <- (1-s2.cat[t])*r[t]
  psm[2,t,6] <- (1-s2.cat[t])*(1-r[t])

  psm[3,t,1] <- s1.oth[t]*psiO[1]
  psm[3,t,2] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[1]
  psm[3,t,3] <- s1.oth[t]*psiO[2]
  psm[3,t,4] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[2]
  psm[3,t,5] <- (1-s1.oth[t])*r[t]
  psm[3,t,6] <- (1-s1.oth[t])*(1-r[t])
  psm[4,t,1] <- 0
  psm[4,t,2] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[1]
  psm[4,t,3] <- 0
  psm[4,t,4] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[2]
  psm[4,t,5] <- (1-s2.oth[t])*r[t]
  psm[4,t,6] <- (1-s2.oth[t])*(1-r[t])
 
  psm[5,t,1] <- 0
  psm[5,t,2] <- 0
  psm[5,t,3] <- 0
  psm[5,t,4] <- 0
  psm[5,t,5] <- 0
  psm[5,t,6] <- 1
  psm[6,t,1] <- 0
  psm[6,t,2] <- 0
  psm[6,t,3] <- 0
  psm[6,t,4] <- 0
  psm[6,t,5] <- 0
  psm[6,t,6] <- 0

  #Recapture
  pom[1,t] <- p1.cat[t]
  pom[2,t] <- p2.cat[t]
  pom[3,t] <- p1.oth[t]
  pom[4,t] <- p2.oth[t]
  pom[5,t] <- 1
  pom[6,t] <- 0
 
}

# Calculate probability of non-observation (dqm) and reshape the        
# array for the observation probabilities  
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
  for (s in 1:mns){
    dpm[s,t,s] <- pom[s,t]
    dqm[s,t,s] <- 1-pom[s,t]
  } # s

  for (s in 1:(mns-1)){
    for (m in (s+1):mns){
      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0
      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0
    } # m
  } # s

  for (s in 2:mns){
    for (m in 1:(s-1)){
      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0
      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0
    } # m
  } # s
} # t

# Define the multinomial likelihood for all released
for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){
  marr[t,1:(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] ~ dmulti(prm[t,], relm[t])
}

# Define cell probabilities of the multistate m-array  
# Define matrix U: product of probabilities of state-transition and
# non-encounter
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){
  Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm
  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){
    Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),
    (j-2)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dqm[,t,]
  } #j
} #t

Um[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm
# Diagonal
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){
  prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <-  
   Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dpm[,t,]
  # Above main diagonal
  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){
    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),
     (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,j,] %*% dpm[,j,]
  } #j
} #t

# Last Diagonal
prm[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <-  
 psm[,n.occasions-1,] %*% dpm[,n.occasions-1,]
# Below main diagonal
for (t in 2:(n.occasions-1)){
  for (j in 1:(t-1)){
    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- zerom
  } #j
} #t

# Last column: probability of non-recapture
for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){
  prm[t,(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] <- 1-sum(prm[t,1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)])
} #t
}

",fill = TRUE)

sink()


inits <- function(){list(mean1.suv.cat=runif(1, 0, 1))}

parameters <- c("mean1.suv.cat", "mean2.suv.cat", "mean1.suv.oth", "mean2.suv.oth",
                "mean1.p.cat", "mean2.p.cat", "mean1.p.oth", "mean2.p.oth",
                "s1.cat","s1.oth","p1.cat","p1.oth",
                "s2.cat","s2.oth","p2.cat","p2.oth","mean.recov", "r", "psiC", "psiO")

ni <- 3000; nb <- 1000; nc <- 3; nt <- 2
model1 <- jags(jags.data, inits, parameters, "marray.jags", n.iter=ni, n.burnin=nb, n.chains=nc, n.thin=nt)

However, I am encountering an error in the model, specifically "Invalid parent values." I suspect this is likely due to a mis-specification in the model, maybe due to how I am modeling the age transitions, though I'm not entirely certain. I've attempted a state-space model, which worked well by considering only the sites and dead recoveries as states (3 states) and incorporating an age matrix as a categorical covariate in the parameters to be estimated.

Nevertheless, I intend to use this multi-state model in an Integrated Population Model (IPM), and with the state-space model, the computation time is exceedingly high, especially when introducing random time effects and temporal covariates.

Is there any aspect I might be overlooking? Your insights would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance,

Diego

parts:
Hi Diego,

 

here are some observations about your model:

  • Since you are using the multinomial likelihood, there is no need to include the recovery process in the state transitions. Therefore, you should remove r[t] from the transitions to state 5, and the transitions from states 1..4 to state 6 must all be 0.
  • The recovery shall be modeled here: pom[5,t] <- r[t]
  • Individuals that are long-time dead (state 6), need to stay there, so the transition from state 6 to 6 must be 1

I have not run the model with these adaptations, so please try and see whether the model runs. If it does still not run, there may be additional issues….

 

Kind regards

 

Michael

El 24 nov 2023, a las 8:15, Michael Schaub <michael...@vogelwarte.ch> escribió:

﻿

Hi Diego,

 

here are some observations about your model:

  • Since you are using the multinomial likelihood, there is no need to include the recovery process in the state transitions. Therefore, you should remove r[t] from the transitions to state 5, and the transitions from states 1..4 to state 6 must all be 0.
  • The recovery shall be modeled here: pom[5,t] <- r[t]
  • Individuals that are long-time dead (state 6), need to stay there, so the transition from state 6 to 6 must be 1

I have not run the model with these adaptations, so please try and see whether the model runs. If it does still not run, there may be additional issues….

 

Kind regards

 

Michael

 

Von: hmec...@googlegroups.com <hmec...@googlegroups.com> Im Auftrag von Diego Arévalo
Gesendet: Donnerstag, 23. November 2023 19:03
An: hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology <hmec...@googlegroups.com>
Betreff: Two age classes in a multi-state model using multinomial likelihood

 

Hello all,

I am currently working on an age-specific multi-state model with multinomial likelihood. The dataset comprises information from >3500 marked vultures of various ages, incorporating recaptures and observations both within and outside our study site, along with dead recoveries spanning 29 occasions. The primary objective is to estimate the site-specific survival rates for two age classes: non-adults (0 to 4 years) and adults (>4 years). The states are encoded as follows: alive as a non-adult at site A (1), alive as an adult at site A (2), alive as a non-adult at site B (3), alive as an adult at site B (4), and recovered dead (5).

Here is the code and .csv:

library(jagsUI) library(IPMbook)

MS <- read.table("CAT_5states.csv", header=T, sep=",")

marr <- marray(MS, unobs = 1)

# Bundle data
# There are 5 states in MS but we added an non-observable state "6"
# to calculate the absorbing state or long-dead state.
mns <- 6
jags.data <- list(marr=marr, n.occasions=ncol(MS), relm=rowSums(marr), mns=mns, zerom=matrix(0, mns, mns),
                  onesm=diag(mns), recap = c(rep(1,3),2:29)) # first two occasions there were no recaptures

sink("marray.jags")
cat("
model {

# Priors and linear models
  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    logit(s1.cat[t]) <- suv1.cat + epsilon1.cat[t]
      epsilon1.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(s2.cat[t]) <- suv2.cat + epsilon2.cat[t]
      epsilon2.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(s1.oth[t]) <- suv1.oth + epsilon1.oth[t]
      epsilon1.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(s2.oth[t]) <- suv2.oth + epsilon2.oth[t]
      epsilon2.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.s)
    logit(p1.cat[t]) <- rec1.cat[recap[t]] + gamma1.cat[recap[t]]
      gamma1.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(p2.cat[t]) <- rec2.cat[recap[t]] + gamma2.cat[recap[t]]
      gamma2.cat[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(p1.oth[t]) <- rec1.oth + gamma1.oth[t]
      gamma1.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(p2.oth[t]) <- rec2.oth + gamma2.oth[t]
      gamma2.oth[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.p)
    logit(r[t]) <- recov + delta[t]
      delta[t] ~ dnorm(0, tau.r)
    F[t] <- mean.F
  }

for (i in 2:(n.occasions-1)){
 rec1.cat[i] <- logit(mean1.p.cat)
 rec2.cat[i] <- logit(mean2.p.cat)
}
 
suv1.cat <- logit(mean1.suv.cat)
suv2.cat <- logit(mean2.suv.cat)
suv1.oth <- logit(mean1.suv.oth)
suv2.oth <- logit(mean2.suv.oth)
rec1.cat[1] <- 0                 #First two occasions on CAT set to 0
rec2.cat[1] <- 0 #First two occasions on OTH set to 0 rec1.oth <- logit(mean1.p.oth)
rec2.oth <- logit(mean2.p.oth)
recov <- logit(mean.recov)
mean1.suv.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean1.suv.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.suv.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.suv.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean1.p.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean1.p.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.p.cat ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean2.p.oth ~ dunif(0, 1)
mean.recov ~ dunif(0, 1)

tau.s <- pow(sigma.s, -2)
sigma.s ~ dunif(0, 10)
sigma2.s <- pow(sigma.s, 2)

tau.p <- pow(sigma.p, -2)
sigma.p ~ dunif(0, 10)
sigma2.p <- pow(sigma.p, 2)

tau.r <- pow(sigma.r, -2)
sigma.r ~ dunif(0, 10)
sigma2.r <- pow(sigma.r, 2)

# Transitions: gamma priors
   for (i in 1:2){
    a[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
    psiC[i] <- a[i]/sum(a[])
    d[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
    psiO[i] <- d[i]/sum(d[])
   }
 
# Define state-transition and re-encounter probabilities
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
  psm[1,t,1] <- s1.cat[t]*psiC[1]
  psm[1,t,2] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[1]
  psm[1,t,3] <- s1.cat[t]*psiC[2]
  psm[1,t,4] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[2]
  psm[1,t,5] <- (1-s1.cat[t])*r[t]
  psm[1,t,6] <- (1-s1.cat[t])*(1-r[t])
  psm[2,t,1] <- 0
  psm[2,t,2] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[1]
  psm[2,t,3] <- 0
  psm[2,t,4] <- s2.cat[t]*psiC[2]
  psm[2,t,5] <- (1-s2.cat[t])*r[t]
  psm[2,t,6] <- (1-s2.cat[t])*(1-r[t])

  psm[3,t,1] <- s1.oth[t]*psiO[1]
  psm[3,t,2] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[1]
  psm[3,t,3] <- s1.oth[t]*psiO[2]
  psm[3,t,4] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[2]
  psm[3,t,5] <- (1-s1.oth[t])*r[t]
  psm[3,t,6] <- (1-s1.oth[t])*(1-r[t])
  psm[4,t,1] <- 0
  psm[4,t,2] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[1]
  psm[4,t,3] <- 0
  psm[4,t,4] <- s2.oth[t]*psiO[2]
  psm[4,t,5] <- (1-s2.oth[t])*r[t]
  psm[4,t,6] <- (1-s2.oth[t])*(1-r[t])
 
  psm[5,t,1] <- 0
  psm[5,t,2] <- 0
  psm[5,t,3] <- 0
  psm[5,t,4] <- 0
  psm[5,t,5] <- 0
  psm[5,t,6] <- 1
  psm[6,t,1] <- 0
  psm[6,t,2] <- 0
  psm[6,t,3] <- 0
  psm[6,t,4] <- 0
  psm[6,t,5] <- 0
  psm[6,t,6] <- 0

  #Recapture
  pom[1,t] <- p1.cat[t]
  pom[2,t] <- p2.cat[t]
  pom[3,t] <- p1.oth[t]
  pom[4,t] <- p2.oth[t]
  pom[5,t] <- 1
  pom[6,t] <- 0
 
}

# Calculate probability of non-observation (dqm) and reshape the        
# array for the observation probabilities  
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
  for (s in 1:mns){
    dpm[s,t,s] <- pom[s,t]
    dqm[s,t,s] <- 1-pom[s,t]
  } # s

  for (s in 1:(mns-1)){
    for (m in (s+1):mns){
      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0
      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0
    } # m
  } # s

  for (s in 2:mns){
    for (m in 1:(s-1)){
      dpm[s,t,m] <- 0
      dqm[s,t,m] <- 0
    } # m
  } # s
} # t

# Define the multinomial likelihood for all released
for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){
  marr[t,1:(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] ~ dmulti(prm[t,], relm[t])
}

# Define cell probabilities of the multistate m-array  
# Define matrix U: product of probabilities of state-transition and
# non-encounter
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){
  Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm
  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){
    Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),
    (j-2)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dqm[,t,]
  } #j
} #t

Um[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <- onesm
# Diagonal
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-2)){
  prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <-  
   Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(t-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,t,] %*% dpm[,t,]
  # Above main diagonal
  for (j in (t+1):(n.occasions-1)){
    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns), (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- Um[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),
     (j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] %*% psm[,j,] %*% dpm[,j,]
  } #j
} #t

# Last Diagonal
prm[(n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns), (n.occasions-2)*mns+(1:mns)] <-  
 psm[,n.occasions-1,] %*% dpm[,n.occasions-1,]
# Below main diagonal
for (t in 2:(n.occasions-1)){
  for (j in 1:(t-1)){
    prm[(t-1)*mns+(1:mns),(j-1)*mns+(1:mns)] <- zerom
  } #j
} #t

# Last column: probability of non-recapture
for (t in 1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)){
  prm[t,(n.occasions*mns-(mns-1))] <- 1-sum(prm[t,1:((n.occasions-1)*mns)])
} #t
}

",fill = TRUE)

sink()


inits <- function(){list(mean1.suv.cat=runif(1, 0, 1))}

parameters <- c("mean1.suv.cat", "mean2.suv.cat", "mean1.suv.oth", "mean2.suv.oth",
                "mean1.p.cat", "mean2.p.cat", "mean1.p.oth", "mean2.p.oth",
                "s1.cat","s1.oth","p1.cat","p1.oth",
                "s2.cat","s2.oth","p2.cat","p2.oth","mean.recov", "r", "psiC", "psiO")

ni <- 3000; nb <- 1000; nc <- 3; nt <- 2
model1 <- jags(jags.data, inits, parameters, "marray.jags", n.iter=ni, n.burnin=nb, n.chains=nc, n.thin=nt)

However, I am encountering an error in the model, specifically "Invalid parent values." I suspect this is likely due to a mis-specification in the model, maybe due to how I am modeling the age transitions, though I'm not entirely certain. I've attempted a state-space model, which worked well by considering only the sites and dead recoveries as states (3 states) and incorporating an age matrix as a categorical covariate in the parameters to be estimated.

Nevertheless, I intend to use this multi-state model in an Integrated Population Model (IPM), and with the state-space model, the computation time is exceedingly high, especially when introducing random time effects and temporal covariates.

Is there any aspect I might be overlooking? Your insights would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance,

Diego
